title: The Bosphorus Brief — 18 September 2026
overview: A heavier news day on the civil-liberties front: a domestic crackdown on LGBTQ+ activists and journalists draws international attention, while European courts and rights bodies keep pressing Ankara on political prisoners. Regionally, the fallout from February's US strikes in Iran continues at the UN, and Turkey has floated a Black Sea de-escalation proposal. Practical items below on money, visas, and safety for residents.
sections:
<section>
<heading>Detentions of LGBTQ+ activists and journalists</heading>
<body>The Guardian reports Turkish authorities detained dozens of LGBTQ+ activists and journalists this week, a story also picked up by BreakingNews.ie. International outlets, including Fox News, frame the action as part of a broader push around "family values," while Turkish state and pro-government outlets have not featured the story in today's material. For foreign residents, this is worth noting mainly as a signal on the current climate around public assembly and speech; there's no indication yet of measures targeting foreign nationals specifically, but those involved in advocacy or reporting should stay informed on legal support channels.</body>
</section>
<section>
<heading>Courts, prisoners, and Europe</heading>
<body>Two rights items matter for the record: Turkey's Constitutional Court found a fair-trial violation in a former officer's coup-related conviction (Stockholm Center for Freedom, opposition-leaning), and the Economist reports Turkey continues to resist European court orders to release certain political prisoners. Neither story is state-media covered today, which is itself worth noting — international and opposition-leaning outlets are carrying this one largely alone. These cases don't directly touch ordinary residency processes, but they're part of the ongoing legal environment around rule-of-law questions that many long-term residents watch closely.</body>
</section>
<section>
<heading>Erdogan confirms 2028 run; regional diplomacy moves</heading>
<body>A senior adviser said President Erdogan will seek re-election in the early-2028 vote (Roya News, Turkish Minute). Separately, Turkey has submitted a proposal to Russia and Ukraine aimed at ending Black Sea attacks (Euronews), and condemned an attempted Houthi drone attack on Mecca (İletişim Başkanlığı, Daily Sabah). Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz's suggestion that Turkey take in Hamas members from Gaza drew notice in opposition-leaning and international coverage; no Turkish government response is in today's material.</body>
</section>
<section>
<heading>Iran strikes: UN findings and pushback</heading>
<body>A UN-backed panel says there are grounds to believe the US committed war crimes in February's strikes on a school in Minab and a sports complex in Lamerd, per the BBC, Bloomberg, Washington Post, and others. The White House has rejected the findings (Middle East Eye). This is a heavy regional story but has no direct bearing on daily life in Turkey; travel advisory levels for Iran remain unchanged at L4.</body>
</section>
<section>
<heading>Money and everyday numbers</heading>
<body>USD/TRY sits at 48.68, EUR/TRY at 56.0, GBP/TRY at 65.35 — worth checking before larger transfers this week. Turkey's finance minister says the Iran conflict added roughly 7 percentage points to inflation (Turkish Minute), useful context if your budgeting has felt tighter than usual. On earthquakes, USGS logged four M4+ events near Turkey and Greece over the past month, including M4.1 near Sulakyurt on September 3 — routine seismic activity for the region, nothing indicating elevated risk.</body>
</section>
</sections>
<closing>Take care out there, and don't forget your umbrella if you're near the Bosphorus this weekend — çay weather is coming.</closing>
